q: 1. In "Full face" method of constructing tunnels, the first operation relates to
options: excavation of one drift in the centre
excavation being done along the periphery
explain: In the full-face tunnelling method, excavation typically begins along the periphery of the tunnel section before removing the central core material.

q: 2. The difference of heights of the tunnels above rail tops of BG and MG tracks is kept
explain: Per railway tunnelling standards, the extra headroom difference between Broad Gauge (BG) and Metre Gauge (MG) tunnel clearances above rail level is typically about 0.60 m.

q: 3. A tunnel is found more advantageous as compared to the alternate routes because it
options: reduces the cost by reducing the route distance and maintenance cost
explain: Tunnels offer multiple advantages simultaneously — protection from snow/weather, shorter route distance (lower operating/maintenance cost), and avoidance of surface right-of-way conflicts.

q: 4. Pick up the correct statement regarding drilling a tunnel from the following
options: Holes are drilled by pneumatically operated rock drills
One drill is required for each 4 to 5 m2 force area
The diameter of the bore hole at the deepest point should be 6 mm more than the diameter of the cartridge
explain: All three statements about tunnel drilling practice — pneumatic drills, drill spacing per face area, and borehole-to-cartridge diameter tolerance — are standard, correct practices.

q: 5. For tunnels exceeding 300 m in length, the grade should be provided below
explain: For long tunnels (>300 m), the design grade is restricted to about 75% of the ruling gradient to ensure safe train operation/ventilation within the tunnel.

q: 6. The method of draining in the tunnels, is generally known as
explain: Tunnel drainage encompasses foredrainage (before construction), dewatering (during construction), and permanent drainage systems (after completion) — all are part of overall tunnel drainage practice.

q: 7. To attain the required shape of the tunnel section, we use
explain: Trimmer holes are drilled around the perimeter of the tunnel face and fired last to trim the section to its exact required shape and profile.

q: 8. Which one of the following methods of tunnelling does not require the use of time bearing
explain: According to the reference book, none of the listed methods (liner plate, shield, compressed air) require timbering support, as they use other structural support systems instead.

q: 9. Forepoling method is generally adopted for tunnelling in :
explain: Forepoling (driving poling boards/plates ahead of excavation) is a supporting technique specifically used in soft, unstable ground to prevent roof collapse ahead of the face.

q: 10. The concentration of the dust particles of the size 0.5 to 5 microns adjacent to the working face should not be more than
explain: Safety standards for tunnel excavation limit the respirable dust concentration (0.5-5 micron particles) near the working face to not more than 400 particles per cm³, to protect worker health.

q: 11. For full face method, the excavation to be done is generally divided into
explain: In the full-face tunnelling method, the face is typically divided into three sections (e.g., top, middle, bottom) to systematize excavation and support work.

q: 12. The tunnels, the artificial underground passages are constructed for :
explain: Tunnels serve a wide range of purposes including highways, railways, and water supply/sewerage conveyance — all valid applications.

q: 13. Railway tunnels, are generally
explain: Railway tunnel cross-sections are commonly designed with a polycentric (multi-centred curved) profile to efficiently accommodate the loading gauge and structural stability requirements.

q: 14. Pick up the explosive used for tunnelling in soft rocks from the following
explain: Ammonia dynamite, being a lower-strength explosive, is suitable for controlled blasting in softer rock formations where excessive shattering must be avoided.

q: 15. Which one of the following methods is generally adopted for tunnelling in firm ground
explain: In firm, self-supporting ground, multiple tunnelling methods (full face, heading and benching, drift) can all be successfully employed since the ground itself provides adequate temporary stability.

q: 16. The length of the needle beam used in needle beam method of tunnelling is usually
explain: In the needle beam method of tunnel support, the needle beams used to temporarily support the crown while excavating below are typically about 5 m to 6 m in length.

q: 17. The underground routes or passages driven through the ground without disturbing overlying soil cover are called
explain: By definition, a tunnel is an underground passage constructed through the ground without disturbing the overlying soil/rock cover, distinguishing it from open-cut excavation.

q: 18. Type of tunnels which are excavated to divert the traffic load of whatsoever type from surface to subsurface routes.
explain: Traffic tunnels are specifically constructed to carry surface transportation (roads, railways, pedestrians) onto subsurface alignments, diverting traffic load underground.

q: 19. In compressed air tunneling, the volume of free air provided is
options: 6m3 per second per m2 of face area
6m3 per minute per m2 of face area
20m3 per minute per m2 of face area
6m3 per hour per m2 of face area
explain: Standard practice for compressed air tunnelling specifies a fresh air supply rate of about 6 cubic metres per minute for each square metre of tunnel face area, ensuring adequate ventilation for workers.

q: 20. Ribs are use for strengthening and stiffening the liner plate for tunnels of diameter greater than
explain: For larger tunnels (diameter exceeding about 3 m), additional steel ribs are used to reinforce and stiffen the liner plates against ground pressure, since the plates alone become insufficient beyond this size.

q: 21. Which of the following methods of tunnelling is used for long tunnels at great depths?
explain: The Austrian (New Austrian Tunnelling Method-related) approach is generally adopted for long, deep tunnels where ground support sequencing and rock mass behaviour are critical.

q: 22. The line at which the tunnel wall breaks from sloping outward can be given as
explain: The spring line marks the point on a tunnel's cross-section where the curved arch/roof portion transitions to the vertical (or sloping) side walls.

q: 23. Which of the following should be considered while aligning a tunnel?
explain: Hydrological conditions (groundwater table, seepage, water-bearing strata) critically affect tunnel alignment decisions, more so than atmospheric or climatic factors at the surface.

q: 24. Which method can be adopted if full face excavation is not possible?
explain: When the full tunnel face cannot be excavated at once (due to size or ground conditions), the heading and benching method — excavating the section in stages — is adopted instead.

q: 25. Tunneling is required in case of .............
explain: Tunneling is specifically employed to create an underground passage, distinct from surface construction.

q: 26. In a compressed air tunneling, the volume of free air provided is .............
options: 6 m3 per second per m2 of face area
6 m3 per minute per m2 of face area
20 m3 per minute per m2 of face area
6 m3 per hour per m2 of face area
explain: Standard practice for compressed air tunneling supplies free air at a rate of about 6 m3 per minute per m2 of tunnel face area.

q: 27. Which of the following lining material is useful for shield driven tunnels in sub aqueous regions?
explain: Cast iron segments provide strong, watertight lining suited for shield-driven tunnels under rivers or water bodies.

q: 28. Circular section of tunnel is not suitable for .............
explain: Per the reference key, circular sections are marked as unsuitable for concrete lining placement in this context, though they are otherwise structurally efficient and widely used with shield methods.

q: 29. If D is the diameter of tunnel in meters, then the thickness of lining in mm as per the empirical formula is given by .............
explain: The empirical formula for tunnel lining thickness commonly used is t = 104D (in mm), where D is the tunnel diameter in meters.

q: 30. Which one of the following tunneling methods is used for laying underground sewers?
explain: The Italian method of tunneling is traditionally associated with constructing underground sewer tunnels.

q: 31. Drifters can be used to drill .............
explain: Drifter drills are versatile machines capable of drilling horizontal, downward, and upward blast holes in tunneling operations.

q: 32. The correct sequence of drilling equipment for increasing size of holes in tunnels is .............
options: wagon drill, churn drill, shot drill
wagon drill, shot drill, churn drill
shot drill, churn drill, wagon drill
churn drill, wagon drill, shot drill
explain: Per standard tunneling practice, hole sizes progressively increase using wagon drill, then shot drill, then churn drill equipment.

q: 33. Which of the following is not a component of the shield?
explain: Liner plates form the permanent tunnel lining installed behind the shield, not a structural component of the shield itself (which includes hood, jacks, and tail).

q: 34. Which of the following methods of tunneling is used for long tunnels at great depths?
explain: The Austrian (New Austrian Tunneling Method) is suited for long tunnels at great depths, using the surrounding rock mass itself for support.

q: 35. The bottom floor of tunnel is called .............
explain: The invert is the term for the bottom floor (base) of a tunnel.
